title: Prompt-Segmentation Meets ROI Encryption: Fine-Grained Video Protection Based on Diffusion Isolation

problem.summary: Region-of-interest (ROI) selective encryption in H.265/HEVC aims to protect sensitive content while preserving the utility of non-ROI regions.
statements: Region-of-interest (ROI) selective encryption in H.265/HEVC aims to protect sensitive content while preserving the utility of non-ROI regions.
Existing coding-unit (CU)-level approaches still suffer from substantial encryption redundancy for two reasons.
First, existing approaches map object-detection bounding boxes to CUs, producing regular rectangular regions, which poorly match the shape of irregular ROI boundaries, such as facial contours.

components: Unauthorized access to these regions creates privacy risks during video transmission, storage, and analysis (Padilla-López, Chaaraoui, and Flórez-Revuelta 2015).
Privacy-preserving video coding must therefore protect sensitive regions while preserving the visual utility of nonsensitive content.
Naive video encryption protects the entire bitstream but also conceals non-sensitive content and incurs unnecessary encryption overhead (Stutz and Uhl 2012).
